purpose: Original anchor and connector grammar for converting separated quilting motifs into continuous-line computerized longarm candidates.

anchors.use: Primary route along a vine, feather spine, scroll stem, or border stem.
anchors.misuse: Do not jump from ornament to ornament when a spine should carry the route.

anchors.use: Entry or exit along a border rail, medallion frame, block frame, or echo line.
anchors.misuse: Do not cross open negative space when the frame can carry travel.

anchors.use: Entry or exit from pearl chains, bead borders, and small circular accent lanes.
anchors.misuse: Do not use pearls to hide random spacing or unrelated jumps.

anchors.use: Quarter-turn transition through corner blocks or border corners.
anchors.misuse: Do not paste a motif into a corner without a designed entry and exit.

anchors.use: Same-plane entry and exit for sashing, narrow borders, and E2E chaining.
anchors.misuse: Do not let a rail wander off baseline unless the design calls for it.

anchors.use: Triangle and setting-piece travel along a diagonal or broad-edge taper.
anchors.misuse: Do not crop a square motif into a triangle and connect the leftovers.

compiler_notes: Use this grammar to choose designed connector styles, not to excuse long exposed travel.
Compile components or geographies first; compiling a full art board into one path is a diagnostic unless the quilt truly stitches as one file.
A generated connector is a candidate stitch path. Human review still decides whether it belongs artistically.
